data.summary: waldenyan.comIt's easy to connect the dots looking back. For me, that line of dots started when I was a kid, spending my time reading random math books and playing with LEGOs. The math texts taught me to seek out truth and objectivity in all the complexity of the world. The plastic bricks fostered a love for building things that were both aesthetically pleasing and functional.In 5th grade I discovered video games and I soon wanted to know how I could build my own. I started on my programming journey with Java as my first language, not knowing where this road would take me. I went from building LEGO contraptions to software programs; no longer was my creativity bounded by physical and material limits. Fascinated by this power, I went on to study the most efficient algorithms and data structures, curious to explore the limits of what computers can do. This curiosity and love for challenges eventually led me to win a gold medal at the International Olympiad in Informatics.Fascinating as computers are though, I have also always been amazed by people. Being a part of many community organizations, I always saw the power of teams to accomplish tasks no individual could. As I learned more about myself and others, I started to find myself at the forefront, helping to guide these groups of people; no longer was my creativity bounded by my own resources and skillset. I realized that with ambition, love for building, and the support of a team and community around you, almost any goal is achievable.My computer science background teaches me how things should optimally be done. My experience as a founder teaches me how things are actually done in a complex world. I love entrepreneurship because it gives me the opportunity to take my vision of a perfect world and help bring it to life. That is why I will always be building products that I believe accelerate the world towards a good future.
